content.user_title: Analyze Research Data with Statistical Guidance
content.value_statement: Choosing tests and reporting results can be slow and error-prone. This skill guides test selection, assumptions, effect sizes, power analysis, Bayesian options, and APA reporting.
actual_capabilities: Selects appropriate hypothesis tests for group comparisons, relationships, and outcome types.
Guides normality, variance, linearity, outlier, and regression diagnostic checks.
Provides Python examples for t-tests, ANOVA, regression, Bayesian tests, and power analysis.
Explains effect sizes, confidence intervals, and practical significance.
Formats statistical results with APA-style wording and required details.
References included guides and an assumption-checking helper script.
limitations: Does not replace a qualified statistician for high-stakes study design or regulated analysis.
Requires users to provide clean data context and verify outputs against their dataset.
Python examples depend on installed packages such as scipy, statsmodels, pingouin, pymc, and arviz.
Does not automatically validate causal claims or research ethics.

use_cases.title: Plan a Study Analysis
use_cases.description: Choose tests, define assumptions, estimate sample size, and plan reporting before data collection.

use_cases.title: Check Statistical Assumptions
use_cases.description: Review normality, variance, outliers, and model diagnostics before interpreting results.

use_cases.title: Prepare Publication Results
use_cases.description: Convert analysis outputs into complete APA-style results with effect sizes and confidence intervals.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner test selection for a clear research question.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a statistical test. My research question is [question]. My outcome variable is [type]. My groups or predictors are [details].

prompt_templates.title: Check Assumptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before running or interpreting a test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the assumptions for [planned test]. My sample size is [n], variables are [variables], and observed issues are [missing data, outliers, or skew].

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting after statistical output is available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret these statistical results in APA style: [test output]. Include assumptions, effect size, confidence interval, and practical significance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Robust Analysis Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a study with multiple analyses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an analysis plan for this study: [design]. Include primary tests, assumption checks, power analysis, multiple comparison handling, and sensitivity analyses.

output_examples.input: A researcher compares two independent groups on a continuous score.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an independent t-test if assumptions hold, Welch correction if variances differ, and Mann-Whitney U for severe non-normality.

output_examples.input: A student has regression output and needs results wording.
output_examples.output: The skill produces an APA-style paragraph with model fit, predictors, confidence intervals, diagnostics, and a plain-language interpretation.

output_examples.input: A team is planning a three-group experiment.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines one-way ANOVA planning, required effect size assumptions, sample size estimation, post-hoc testing, and reporting details.

best_practices: State the research question, study design, variable types, and planned comparisons before choosing tests.
Check assumptions and diagnostics before interpreting p-values or model coefficients.
Report effect sizes, intervals, exact p-values, and non-significant planned analyses.
anti_patterns: Do not test many alternatives until one result is significant.
Do not treat statistical significance as practical importance.
Do not omit assumption violations, transformations, or excluded observations.

faq.question: Can this skill choose a statistical test for my study?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your research question, variable types, group structure, and sampling design.

faq.question: Does it run analysis automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and Python examples. Users must run code in their own environment and verify results.

faq.question: Can it help with APA-style reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes reporting templates for tests, models, assumptions, effect sizes, and intervals.

faq.question: Does it support Bayesian statistics?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Bayesian alternatives, priors, Bayes Factors, credible intervals, and convergence checks.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide variable names, measurement scales, sample sizes, group definitions, missing data notes, and analysis output when available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated or clinical decisions?
faq.answer: Use it as support only. High-stakes, regulated, or clinical analyses require qualified statistical review.
